title: The Last Broadcast
subtitle: Ninety seconds that were never live
briefing: A late-night presenter, Nora Bell, dies in her studio during a live broadcast. The programme continues for ninety seconds after the time of death established by the pathologist. Four people were in the building. The studio door logs one entry and one exit, both accounted for. The desk recording is intact and unedited.
solution: Aksel Ranta, the station's technical director, had been blackmailing Nora over a recording he held. When she told him on air that she intended to say so, he cut the live feed and substituted ninety seconds of a rehearsal recording, entering the studio during the substitution. The struggle that followed was not intended to kill her. The desk recording is intact because it records the output, not the microphone.

topics.that_hour: where they were between ten and eleven

suspects.name: Aksel Ranta
suspects.motive: Held a recording he had been using to control her for a year.

statements.question: Where were you between ten and eleven?
statements.text: In the gallery, watching the levels. I did not leave it.

statements.question: Was there a break in the live feed?
statements.text: There was no break. The output is continuous, and I can prove it.

statements.question: What recording did she mean?
statements.text: I have no idea what she was referring to. She said a great many things on air.

suspects.name: Deirdre Okonjo
suspects.motive: Had argued with Nora about the programme's direction that evening.

statements.question: Where were you between ten and eleven?
statements.text: In the gallery until twenty past, then the edit suite.

statements.question: Was there a break in the live feed?
statements.text: Something felt wrong around half ten. The room tone changed and then it did not.

statements.question: What recording did she mean?
statements.text: She told me last week that somebody had something of hers. She would not say who.

suspects.name: Ben Croft
suspects.motive: Was in the studio corridor at the relevant time.

statements.question: Where were you between ten and eleven?
statements.text: In the corridor and the rack room, chasing an intermittent fault.

statements.question: Was there a break in the live feed?
statements.text: The desk did not show one. But the rack log has something at 10:31.

statements.question: What recording did she mean?
statements.text: No idea. I keep out of the presenters' business.

suspects.name: Hallam Pike
suspects.motive: Nora had criticised him on air three weeks earlier.

statements.question: Where were you between ten and eleven?
statements.text: I left at five past ten. The door log will show it and so will the taxi.

statements.question: Was there a break in the live feed?
statements.text: I was in a car by then. I heard the programme on the radio.

statements.question: What recording did she mean?
statements.text: I do not know and I would rather not speculate.

timeline.text: The studio guest leaves the building.
The presenter refers on air to a recording she intends to discuss.
The studio door records one entry.
The transmission source is switched back.
The presenter is found in the studio.

hints: The output recording is intact. Ask what the output is a recording of.
Ninety seconds of a live programme were not live.
Somebody had something of hers. Find out where it was kept.
